verification: Recorded from a run of the procedure above observed on 2026-07-24 at repository commit f57e23be8dd8e70f2ba9fb0d63fdf0192e5b9093, and reproduced by scripts/check_rust.py in the same session. trybuild compared each fixture against the retained .stderr byte for byte and all four compile-fail and two compile-pass cases passed, so every diagnostic field below describes text the pinned compiler was seen to emit rather than transcribed text. The adr_clause fields quote docs/decisions/0067-use-pinned-nightly-dependent-static-shapes.md with its hard line wrapping removed; verify_claims.py resolves the reference but not the wording.

claims.adr_clause: Rust evidence remains non-authoritative, explicitly weakenable, checked on refinement, and excluded from semantic, compilation, artifact, and cache identity.
claims.statement: Field privacy stops a consumer building ShapedValue directly, so evidence can only be attached by Builder::refine after the graph has checked it. Weakening is explicit; forging is not available at all.
claims.first_line: error[E0451]: fields `value` and `evidence` of struct `ShapedValue` are private

claims.adr_clause: Implementing the production `tiler-ir` now implements the selected family as sealed evidence checked by builder- and program-owned refinement.
claims.statement: ShapeEvidence is sealed by a private supertrait, so downstream code cannot claim an evidence class the graph never checked, and StaticShape is reported as the only implementor.
claims.first_line: error[E0277]: the trait bound `Forged: nightly_shape_api::sealed::Sealed` is not satisfied
required_fragments: the trait `nightly_shape_api::sealed::Sealed` is not implemented for `Forged`

claims.adr_clause: A mismatched rank and array length is not representable as a Rust type.
claims.statement: The dependent array const parameter makes the extent array's length depend on RANK, so StaticShape<2, { [2, 3, 4] }> is rejected by type checking at the alias rather than by a later admission check.
required_fragments: expected an array with a size of 2, found one with a size of 3

claims.adr_clause: Rust's intended const-generics model is a closer architectural match: constant values participate structurally in type identity.
claims.statement: Two same-rank shapes whose extents differ only in order do not unify, so an axis-order error at a call site is an ordinary type error naming both extent vectors. This is the compile-fail contrast the cross-crate identity case is measured against.

claims.adr_clause: Exact static evidence supports arbitrary rank through one canonical family.
claims.statement: Ranks 0, 1, 2, and 64 instantiate the same zero-sized StaticShape family, so the arbitrary-rank claim is exercised at both ends rather than at the matrix rank alone.

claims.adr_clause: Equivalent extent arrays no longer depend on which crate named a descriptor.
claims.statement: A literal alias, a const-fed alias, a reexport, an alias in a second independent crate, and a proc-macro-generated alias all name one type, which is the property downstream descriptor families could not provide.
